clue.text: See 26
Strong, short stick has snapped

indicators.note: short means the word for stick loses its final letter, cut down

parts.note: a rod is a stick
bust means broken, snapped

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a sturdy-looking stubby stick has broken anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust and strong are synonyms describing something sturdy and hard to break.

clue.text: Thin poles on top of edifice

parts.note: spars are poles, as on a ship's rigging

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Slender poles sit on the roof of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly spread, so it is a synonym of thin as in a thin crowd.

clue.text: Attention-grabber last seen in Tennessee, however touring California with singer

indicators.note: says to take only the final letter of the word that follows
touring means going round, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: yet means however
Cher is the American pop singer

explanation.surface: A travel story: a singer touring California, with Tennessee last on the itinerary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eye-catching draws the gaze, so an eye-catcher is literally an attention-grabber.

clue.text: Right to tuck one in for a late snooze

indicators.note: to tuck something in is to put it inside, so one piece goes into another
completes the phrase tuck in, signalling insertion into the word for right

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone claims the right to tuck themselves in for a lazy morning nap.
explanation.walkthrough: A lien is a legal claim over someone's property.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is staying in bed late in the morning, a late snooze in the British idiom.

clue.text: Somewhat facing gun

parts.note: at can mean facing or directed toward, as in looking at
a rifle is a gun

explanation.surface: A cryptic two-word scene: being somewhat in front of a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom a trifle means slightly, a little, which matches somewhat.

clue.text: TV presenters Dec ___ in love, moving quite slowly

parts.note: the British TV duo Ant and Dec; with Dec put first, the blank is filled by the words and Ant
love is nil in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quiz about a TV duo, the pair in love and moving slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a famous British TV presenting duo; reading 'Dec and Ant' fills the blank with AND ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a musical tempo marking meaning a little faster than andante, a fairly slow pace.

clue.text: Grass or speed

explanation.surface: A choice between two words, grass or speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a marsh plant like grass and the act of hurrying at speed.

clue.text: Half of a half, say, overcoming monarch in controversial underground operations

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming means sitting above, so this piece comes first
says to keep only the first half of the word given

parts.note: a half is an example of a fraction
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A sentence about dividing something, with a monarch overcome amid controversial digging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a half as an example of a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Fracking is hydraulic fracturing for shale gas, contentious drilling work below ground.

clue.text: Intertwine ground net and fish

indicators.note: ground as the past of grind means crushed, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: An angler's instruction: tangle the net on the ground and go fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle things is to twist them together, an intertwining.

clue.text: See 26
Stripper in ecstasy I'd fooled around with

indicators.note: fooling around messes things about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A racy confession about fooling around with a stripper while on ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecdysiast is a jocular formal word for a striptease artist, coined by H. L. Mencken.

clue.text: Dyer's work around America is holding up

indicators.note: the dyeing word wraps around the abbreviation for America

parts.note: a dyer stains cloth, so the work is staining

explanation.surface: A craft report: the dyer's business across America is keeping going.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustaining something means supporting or bearing its weight, holding it up.

clue.text: Surface broke, though not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: skint is British slang for broke, penniless

explanation.surface: Something has cracked on the surface but not right through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' looks like a verb about breaking; it means short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin is the outer layer of something, its surface, as on milk or paint.

clue.text: Fluid arrives carrying first of buffalo over in area of drained land

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so what comes before sits on top
carrying means holding, so the reshuffled letters hold the next piece
something fluid has no fixed shape, so the letters of the next word are rearranged
take just the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Floodwater arrives with a buffalo swept along in a low-lying region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid' rearranges ARRIVES as RIVERAS, which carries B (the first of 'buffalo') to give RIVERBAS, all over IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A river basin is the whole region of land whose water runs off into one river and its tributaries.

clue.text: Tory laid into liberal, being dependent

parts.note: con is short for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: liberal means free, not strict, so the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A political spat: a Tory laying into a Liberal, out of reliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' sounds political but signals the anagram of LAID INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditional means hinging on something else, as an offer depends on terms.

clue.text: Brown in town, unsettled as deputy

indicators.note: the colour word goes inside the reshuffled letters
unsettled means disturbed, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: umber is a brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: Mr Brown arrives in town, uneasy in his role as second-in-command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname but is the earth pigment, placed in the reshuffle of TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A number two is the second in command, the deputy to a leader.

clue.text: Sea a tad icy in reality, starts out cold

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the gathered letters are reshuffled
starts means the opening letters of each of the words that precede it

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A traveller reports that the sea is, in reality, slightly icy and starts off cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes IIR from 'icy in reality'; 'out' mixes those with A and TAD to give ADRIATI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic is the arm of the Mediterranean between Italy and the Balkans, a named body of salt water.

clue.text: See 28
10 player in fanciful Midlands fen, say?

parts.note: Dudley is a town in the West Midlands of England

indicators.note: say signals the word sounds the same as what is written

parts.note: a fen is boggy land, like a moor

explanation.surface: An imagined fen in the Midlands, offered as a whimsical place name.
explanation.walkthrough: Dudley is a town in England's West Midlands; 'in fanciful' marks the made-up place name Dudley Moor. The film '10' (1979) starred Dudley Moore.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudley Moore was the lead in the 1979 Blake Edwards comedy film called '10'.

clue.text: Old Kenyan revolutionaries, two paws cut

indicators.note: two means the shortened word is written twice
cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to maul is to paw roughly

explanation.surface: A grim note about two paws being cut, set against Kenyan rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mau Mau were insurgents who rose against British colonial rule in Kenya in the 1950s.

clue.text: False name, that is, for villain

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters of the word are faked into a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A villain operating under a false name.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is a mean, nasty person, the bad guy in childish terms.

clue.text: US composer into percussive sounds

indicators.note: into means the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An American composer who was into drums and percussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was a modernist American composer of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Washington pop group good for stuffing trimmed green vegetable

indicators.note: the pieces before are used as stuffing, placed inside the trimmed word
trimmed means the outer letters are cut off

parts.note: DC, District of Columbia, is the US capital Washington
Abba is the Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: A cooking scene: Washington stuffing a pop group's greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington' is the US capital, DC, not the president; 'trimmed' takes the outer letters off 'green'.
explanation.definitionFit: Red cabbage is a purple-leaved variety of cabbage, a common vegetable.

clue.text: Might meat be better?

parts.note: better as healed and meat as preserved: one word describes both a recovered patient and salted ham

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether the meat could be improved.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both made well again and preserved by salting or smoking, as meat is.

clue.text: Honey at a premium

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment, like sweetheart

explanation.surface: Honey is costly these days.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an affectionate address and a description of something costly.

clue.text: Examiner biting lip in term time

indicators.note: biting means taking into the mouth, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a tester examines
a rim is a lip or edge

explanation.surface: An examiner bites their lip during the school term.
explanation.definitionFit: In some school systems an academic term is a third of the year, one of three periods.

clue.text: Actor's interpretation of Lear, no less, sublime

indicators.note: an interpretation of a text reworks it, so these words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A critic praises an actor's take on King Lear as nothing short of sublime.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Actor' is just a link. Sir Simon Russell Beale is an English stage actor who did play Lear, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Russell Beale is a celebrated British stage and screen performer, so he is an example of an actor.

clue.text: Final word, taking a penny off inexpensive English port

indicators.note: off means the next words' letters are removed

parts.note: cheap means inexpensive
a with P, the abbreviation for penny
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A traveller's farewell after saving a penny on a cheap trip to an English port.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEAP loses AP to leave CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British goodbye, the last thing said when parting.

clue.text: I have endured set slipping around — might this fix it?

indicators.note: a set of teeth slipping around is unsteady, so these letters move into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A denture wearer has suffered loose false teeth and asks for a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'set' is a set of false teeth, and 'it' in the definition refers back to that loose set.
explanation.definitionFit: Denture adhesive is a paste that holds false teeth firmly in place, a fix for a slipping set.
